analysis: The fluidity of the plasma membrane is influenced by the types of fatty acids and other molecules incorporated into it. Arachidonic acid, being an unsaturated fatty acid, introduces kinks in the phospholipid bilayer due to its double bonds, which prevents the tight packing of lipid molecules, thereby increasing membrane fluidity. Cholesterol, although it plays a dual role, generally tends to stabilize the membrane structure and can decrease fluidity at higher concentrations. Saturated fatty acids like palmitic acid and stearic acid lack double bonds, which allows them to pack closely together, increasing membrane rigidity and decreasing fluidity. Based on standard medical knowledge and the consensus on the effects of these molecules on membrane properties, arachidonic acid is the most likely to increase membrane fluidity.
